shell_err_locked_cmd: This command is not available in this mission: {cmd}
puzzle_match_title: Connect the pairs (tap left, then right)
puzzle_password_title: Build the password from the clues
puzzle_codefix_title: Tap the wrong line and pick a replacement
mission_broken: This mission can't be opened right now
m1_01_brief_1: Hi, rookie. I'm Ghost. Your first job is an easy one.
m1_01_brief_2: There's a welcome note on the cafe PC down the street. Find it with scan, get in with connect, read it with open.
m1_01_done_1: Good. Three commands and you can go anywhere. The next one gets more interesting.
m1_01_f_readme: My laptop. To do: try connecting to the cafe PC.
m1_01_f_welcome: Welcome! You just connected to your first server.
m1_01_hint_1: Tap scan first to find nearby servers.
m1_01_hint_2: Tap connect, then tap the server name chip.
m1_02_brief_1: A friend forgot the password to their vault server. They left a note, but wrote it in code.
m1_02_brief_2: Read the note on my laptop and crack the coded file with decode. Then use that password to get into vault-box.
m1_02_done_1: One decode and the code falls apart. Your friend is bad at security. On to the next job.
m1_02_f_note: The password is in secret.txt, but I shifted every letter three places. The decode command should undo it.
m1_02_f_key: Vault key number: 4417. Please pass it to my friend.
m1_02_hint_1: Read note.txt first. It says which file to decode.
m1_02_hint_2: Tap decode and pick secret.txt to reveal the real password.
m1_02_hint_3: Run connect vault-box, then type the decoded word exactly.
m1_03_brief_1: The router admin page is locked. It only opens once the back-panel ports are wired correctly.
m1_03_brief_2: My laptop note says what plugs into each port. Match them up exactly.
m1_03_done_1: Wiring sorted. The admin note is yours now.
m1_03_f_note: Router back panel: PWR takes the 5V adapter, LAN1 the 192.168.0.2 desktop, WAN the ISP line, USB the mouse.
m1_03_f_admin: Admin note: change the router password next week.
m1_03_hint_1: note.txt lists what connects to each port.
m1_03_hint_2: connect router opens the wiring puzzle. Tap a left port, then its partner on the right.
m1_03_hint_3: PWR→5V, LAN1→192.168.0.2, WAN→ISP, USB→mouse, then open admin.txt.
m1_04_brief_1: A cloud drive is locked and its owner can't remember the password. Luckily there are clues.
m1_04_brief_2: People usually mix a pet's name with a year. Check the photo note on my laptop.
m1_04_done_1: A pet's name, of course. People make the same mistake every time.
m1_04_f_photo: Note on the back of a photo: our cat Momo (momo). We brought her home in spring 2019.
m1_04_f_diary: Diary: Finally got back into the drive. I'll write the password down this time.
m1_04_p1_c1: The cat's name, in lowercase English.
m1_04_p1_c2: Then the year she came home, in four digits.
m1_04_hint_1: photo.txt has the cat's name and the year.
m1_04_hint_2: connect cloud-drive opens the build puzzle. Tap the name piece, then the year piece.
m1_05_brief_1: An old server won't start. It's an antique that needs its boot order set by hand.
m1_05_brief_2: I put the manual on my laptop. Drag the steps into order and it should come alive.
m1_05_done_1: The antique lives. Good job grabbing the backup file.
m1_05_f_manual: Old server boot order: 1) power on 2) load the BIOS 3) start the OS 4) log in.
m1_05_f_backup: Backup list: 1,204 photos, 88 documents. All safe.
m1_05_hint_1: manual.txt lists the boot order by number.
m1_05_hint_2: connect old-server opens the order puzzle. Long-press an item and drag it.
m1_05_hint_3: Power on → Load BIOS → Start OS → Login, then open backup.txt.
m1_06_brief_1: This one is a real request. Before she passed, a grandmother left a gift for her grandson on a safe server.
m1_06_brief_2: You need the mail server first to learn how to open the safe. The mail password is coded on my laptop.
m1_06_brief_3: There are two servers, so if you get lost, use back. Use everything you've learned.
m1_06_done_1: The grandson got his gift. That's the end of your first chapter.
m1_06_done_2: From now on, no more toy commands. Real ones. Get ready.
m1_06_f_note: Mail server password is in hint.txt, each letter shifted by one. How to open the safe is in the mail.
m1_06_f_letter: To my grandson. Set the color locks: red to A, blue to C, green to B. To open it, turn the key first, open the lid, then take the gift.
m1_06_f_prize: The gift: a map to the tree Grandma planted in your name.
m1_06_hint_1: Read note.txt and decode hint.txt. That's the mail-box password.
m1_06_hint_2: letter.txt on mail-box has the color pairs and the safe's opening order.
m1_06_hint_3: red→A, blue→C, green→B. Then Turn key → Open lid → Take prize.
title_tagline: Every server has a back door
m2_01_brief_1: No more toys. From here on, these are the commands real servers use. ls shows what's in a folder, cat reads a file.
m2_01_brief_2: Read the menu file on the neighborhood cafe's server. It's cat now, not open.
m2_01_done_1: ls and cat. With those two you can read half the files in the world.
m2_01_f_readme: Request from the cafe owner. Check the menu file before the server inspection.
m2_01_f_menu: Today's menu: Americano, latte, mocha. The owner will buy you a latte when the inspection is done.
m2_01_hint_1: After connect, tap ls to see the file names.
m2_01_hint_2: Tap cat, then tap the file name chip.
m2_02_brief_1: The owner's memo is somewhere deep on the server. Use cd to enter folders, and pwd to see where you are if you get lost.
m2_02_brief_2: Folders named after people usually live under home.
m2_02_done_1: Folders are boxes inside boxes. cd goes in, cd .. comes out. Get used to it.
m2_02_f_readme: Memo location: somewhere in the owner's personal folder.
m2_02_f_memo: Owner's memo: switch coffee bean suppliers next month. The password notebook is in the safe.
m2_02_hint_1: Check the folder list with ls, then cd into home.
m2_02_hint_2: There's an owner folder inside home. Run ls there.
m2_02_hint_3: cd home → cd owner → cat memo.txt
m2_03_brief_1: The POS terminal is locked and nobody knows the password. But someone once typed it into the wrong box instead of the login screen.
m2_03_brief_2: Mistakes like that end up in the log as ERROR. grep shows only the lines containing a word. Logs live under var/log.
m2_03_done_1: Logs don't lie. One grep pulled a single line out of thousands.
m2_03_f_readme: The POS password should be somewhere in the shop-server logs.
m2_03_f_report: Daily sales report: normal. Change the POS password today.
m2_03_hint_1: On shop-server, go in with cd var, then cd log.
m2_03_hint_2: grep ERROR app.log shows the line with the mistake.
m2_03_hint_3: The text after pw= is the pos-terminal password.
m2_04_brief_1: The owner hid an important memo on the server and forgot where.
m2_04_brief_2: Files whose names start with a dot (.) don't show up in ls. ls -a shows everything.
m2_04_done_1: A hidden file is still a file. One -a and you see it all.
m2_04_f_readme: Find the hidden memo. Look for a file that starts with a dot.
m2_04_f_secret: Hidden memo: the safe password notebook is in the second drawer. Don't tell anyone.
m2_04_hint_1: Plain ls won't show it. Add the -a chip to ls.
m2_04_hint_2: A file name starting with a dot will appear.
m2_05_brief_1: The backup NAS is locked. The manager who set the password quit. Luckily they left a note in the staff folder.
m2_05_brief_2: People always make passwords the same way. Read the note and build it.
m2_05_done_1: A dog's name plus its birth year. Half the passwords out there look like this.
m2_05_f_readme: backup-nas password clue: the staff folder on shop-server.
m2_05_f_notes: Manager's note: the NAS password is our dog Bori's name (bori) followed by the year Bori was born, 2021.
m2_05_p1_c1: The dog's name, in lowercase English.
m2_05_hint_1: There's a notes.txt in shop-server's staff folder.
m2_05_hint_2: connect backup-nas opens the build puzzle.
m2_06_brief_1: Last job of the chapter. The owner forgot both the ledger server password and the office PC password.
m2_06_brief_2: The office PC password should be in the server's access log, and the ledger server opens with the wiring notes on the office PC.
m2_06_brief_3: You'll be moving between three servers. Everything you've learned.
m2_06_done_1: Ledger recovered. The owner is offering you free lattes for life.
m2_06_done_2: From the next chapter the keyboard opens up. You'll type for real, like a real terminal.
m2_06_f_keys: Ledger server wiring: USB to keyboard, HDMI to monitor, LAN to switch, PWR to 12V.
m2_06_f_ledger: Ledger: May sales normal. All safe.
m2_06_hint_1: On shop-server, grep owner in var/log/access.log.
m2_06_hint_2: Once inside office-pc, desk/keys.txt has the wiring pairs.
m2_06_hint_3: USB→keyboard, HDMI→monitor, LAN→switch, PWR→12V. Then cat ledger.txt.
m3_01_brief_1: From now on you type. The chips are still there, but typing a whole path is much faster.
m3_01_brief_2: find searches files by part of their name and tells you the full path. Type that path right after cat.
m3_01_done_1: The moment you typed a path by hand, you became a terminal user.
m3_01_f_readme: Starting the company file server audit. Begin with the beta project notes.
m3_01_f_notes: Beta project notes: schedule slipped two weeks. Reason is in the audit report.
m3_01_hint_1: Type find notes to get the full path.
m3_01_hint_2: Type cat followed by the whole path, starting from /.
m3_02_brief_1: The budget file is somewhere, but there are dozens of folders. No time to open them one by one.
m3_02_brief_2: All we know is the name contains budget. Give find just that piece.
m3_02_done_1: One line instead of digging through ten folders. That's why people use the terminal.
m3_02_f_readme: Find the final budget. Name contains budget.
m3_02_hint_2: Read the path it prints with cat.
m3_03_brief_1: An employee's laptop is locked and they're on vacation. The password reset token should be in the auth log.
m3_03_brief_2: The log is long. Send what cat reads into grep with |, and only the lines you want remain: cat file | grep word
m3_03_done_1: A pipe is a tube between commands. The left side's output flows to the right.
m3_03_f_readme: jkim-laptop password: left as a token in logs/auth.log on corp-fs.
m3_03_f_findings: Audit note: two login attempts from an outside IP. Recommend an account lockout policy.
m3_03_hint_2: The text after token= is the jkim-laptop password.
m3_04_brief_1: ssh connects as account@server. If the account is wrong, the server won't let you in.
m3_04_brief_2: Which admin account belongs to which server is written in staff.txt on the file server.
m3_04_done_1: Get one account name wrong and nothing works. Type exactly what's written.
m3_04_f_readme: Check the db-server dump. The account is in staff.txt on corp-fs.
m3_04_hint_1: staff.txt on corp-fs has the db-server account name.
m3_05_brief_1: Nobody knows where the admin who quit moved things. But the terminal remembers what was typed.
m3_05_brief_2: Type history to see the commands typed on that server. Follow them.
m3_05_f_readme: Find the moved file. Start with history on corp-fs.
m3_05_f_secret: The previous admin's handover document. Fully recovered.
m3_05_hint_1: Type history on corp-fs to see an ssh command.
m3_05_hint_2: Type that ssh command as is, then cat the path scp sent the file to.
m3_06_brief_1: Last case of the internal audit. The evidence is on the vault server, and the vault password has something to do with the CEO's coffee order.
m3_06_brief_2: The HR server account is in the file server's history, the order records are in the HR server's payroll folder. Inside the vault is a map to the next server.
m3_06_done_1: Evidence secured. The audit report goes out under your name.
m3_06_done_2: Next chapter is code. Read it, fix it, run it.
m3_06_f_readme: Order: corp-fs history → hr-box → vault-01 → archive-02.
m3_06_f_notes: Vault password hint: the drink the CEO always orders (lowercase, no spaces or hyphens) followed by the number of their first order.
m3_06_f_map: archive-02 lock: north is mountain, east is sea, south is city, west is forest.
m3_06_p1_c1: Write the drink name in lowercase, no spaces or hyphens.
m3_06_p1_c2: Then the CEO's first order number (digits only).
m3_06_hint_1: grep ceo in hr-box's payroll/orders.log. The first order number goes at the end of the password.
m3_06_hint_2: map.txt on vault-01 is the answer to the archive-02 matching puzzle.
